tier_reason: First-party README Benchmarks table (i7-6700K: 200 ns / 350 MB/s Windows, 280 ns / 465 MB/s Linux) with no compiler, flags or stored results for those runs; the 2500 ns naive-logger baseline is an estimate (quoted ~1500 ns write() plus an assumed 1000 ns of formatting), not a measured run. test.cpp holds latency and write() benches but no results, so C.

corrections.caveats: The baseline is hypothetical, not a measured run: the 2500 ns figure adds a quoted ~1500 ns write() cost to an assumed 1000 ns of formatting. test.cpp does time a 5-byte write() (BenchFileWriteLatency, 200000 iterations) and the logger latency modes (raw, simple fmt, param fmt; 50000 messages after 100 warmup into a 32 MB ring sized never to stall), but no result file is stored and the README numbers name no compiler or flags. test.cpp also has a 'spd comparison' benchmark that only times 1M uberlog Info() calls and contains no spdlog code; there are no spdlog numbers anywhere in the repo. Third-party logging shootouts found (MuggleWei cc_log_benchmark) do not list uberlog. Latency counts only the in-program cost, not the writer process's work. README itself says a naive logger is fine below many thousands of messages per second, and the 2018 Meltdown/KPTI benefit is 'not measured'. The seed lead (from a C++ book) says it is not as fast as specialized low-latency loggers. No commits since 2020-04-08 (over 6 years); no releases.

notes: README, LICENSE (MIT, IMQS Software 2016), build script (clang++ -O2 -ggdb -std=c++11) and test.cpp benches checked; repo page shows 18 stars, 10 forks, 68 commits, last commit Apr 8 2020. Record accurate apart from the age wording in caveats.

tier_reason: The only Rayon-vs-OpenMP numbers are in the competing Fork Union README (benchmark code public in scripts/nbody.{cpp,rs} and scripts/propagation.{cpp,rs}, flags -O3 -march=native / target-cpu=native stated), but no compiler or version is named for the tables and CPUs are families only (Intel SPR, RPL, Apple M5 Pro, Graviton 5), so not A; a competitor library's README is not a well-known independent benchmark suite (precedent: TurboPFor README numbers run by a competitor's author were tiered C), and Rayon beats OpenMP only in a minority of cells.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Mixed, mostly OpenMP ahead. Rayon wins: N-body on the 24x Intel RPL Windows box, Rayon 151 / 151 us vs OpenMP 360 / 627 us (about 2.4x static, 4.2x dynamic, derived from page data); connected components with dynamic (one-vertex) scheduling, Rayon vs OpenMP GTEPS 6.5 vs 0.4 on 128x Intel SPR (about 16x, derived from page data), 6.2 vs 0.4 on 192x Graviton 5 (about 15x, derived from page data), 5.2 vs 0.1 on 24x Intel RPL (about 50x from rounded values, derived from page data); static connected components on 18x Apple M5 Pro 23.8 vs 23.0 (about 1.03x, derived from page data). Rayon loses: N-body on M5 Pro 222 / 339 us vs 115 / 137, on SPR 483 / 739 vs 115 / 226, on Graviton 5 490 / 580 vs 266 / 216; dynamic connected components on M5 Pro 14.6 vs 18.3 GTEPS; static connected components on SPR 8.5 vs 28.2, on Graviton 5 8.4 vs 53.9, on RPL 9.4 vs 11.4.
corrections.workload: Fork Union README Performance section: N-body at 512 bodies on every logical core (microseconds per iteration, static / dynamic) and connected components by label propagation on a ~27M-edge R-MAT 'necklace' graph (GTEPS, 84 fork-join rounds per pass), one fixed 30-second window per cell, four machines. Rayon static is par_chunks_mut with one stripe per worker in N-body and plain par_iter_mut (Rayon's default adaptive splitting) in connected components; Rayon dynamic is par_iter_mut().with_max_len(1). OpenMP uses schedule(static) and schedule(dynamic, 1).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: C++ side: Release build adds -O3 -march=native -mtune=native and -ffp-contract=off (scripts/CMakeLists.txt), no LTO; OpenMP is -fopenmp (libgomp) under GCC and Homebrew libomp under Clang/AppleClang (OpenMP is disabled for Clang without Homebrew). The compiler used for each machine is not stated; the README names MinGW-GCC for the 24x i9 (RPL) Windows box, and the macOS instructions use Homebrew LLVM clang plus libomp. N-body runs under numactl --interleave=all with OMP_PROC_BIND=spread OMP_PLACES=cores per the scripts/nbody.cpp header; connected-components cells run bare without pinning per the scripts/propagation.{cpp,rs} headers. Rust side: cargo build --release with RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=native', profile opt-level 3, lto false, codegen-units 1, unchecked hot loops, rayon '1.11' requirement in Cargo.toml.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 13.4k stars, 618 forks; rayon 1.12.0 published on crates.io 2026-04-14
corrections.caveats: Evidence is a side result of a competing library's benchmark: the README belongs to Fork Union (ForkUnion, Rust and C++), whose author promotes it as about 3-6x faster than OpenMP and 12-16x faster than Rayon, so the figures were not produced by the Rayon project. Rayon beats OpenMP only in a minority of cells; OpenMP's 'dynamic' columns use schedule(dynamic, 1), a one-vertex grain whose shared queue collapses at high thread counts (0.1-0.4 GTEPS, as the README itself explains), which is why the 15-50x Rayon wins appear; against OpenMP's static schedule Rayon is behind on most machines (up to 6.4x lower GTEPS on Graviton 5, derived from page data) and it also loses dynamic connected components on the M5 Pro. The one N-body win is on the Windows box where the README names MinGW-GCC, so the OpenMP runtime there is probably libgomp, not libomp. Fork Union's documentation disagrees on fast-math: the scripts/nbody.cpp and nbody.rs headers say the C++ build adds -ffast-math, while scripts/CMakeLists.txt says strict IEEE math is deliberate and adds only -ffp-contract=off; which build produced the tables is not stated. Rayon 'static' in connected components is plain par_iter_mut with adaptive splitting, not a fixed per-worker stripe as the doc comment says. Exact CPU models and compiler versions are not given, and the benchmark does not use the cited 'oneTBB parallel_for' or 'std::execution::par' baselines. Rayon's own repo has no comparison against OpenMP, TBB or std::execution::par: the README carries no numbers, PR #1156 (par_sort sync) says 'mostly the same or slightly better' with no figures, and rayon-demo prints sequential-vs-parallel speedups at run time without stored results. A search snippet (arXiv 2502.15536, NPB-Rust, page blocked and not opened) reports Rayon slower than C++ OpenMP on the NAS kernels; snippet only.

notes: All table numbers match the Fork Union README rows for Rayon and OpenMP; the record missed the M5 Pro dynamic connected-components loss and misattributed 'LLVM clang plus libomp' and '-ffast-math' as the general C++ build (CMake uses GCC libgomp or Homebrew libomp and states strict IEEE). Consider decision keep with shortcoming 'not faster than OpenMP in most cells'; Fork Union itself was tiered C in batch-44.
